title: Food delivery startup Wonder files for IPO as it explores its next big bite

claims.claim: Food delivery startup Wonder filed confidentially for an initial public offering on Thursday.

evidence.quote: Food delivery startup Wonder is moving closer to becoming a publicly traded company after confidentially filing for an initial public offering (IPO). The company announced the filing on Thursday

claims.claim: Wonder was founded in 2018 by entrepreneur Marc Lore.

evidence.quote: Founded in 2018 by entrepreneur Marc Lore, Wonder has evolved from a food delivery concept into a broader food technology business.

claims.claim: In July, Wonder announced it had raised more than $650 million in a funding round valuing the company at around $9 billion.

evidence.quote: Those ambitions gained further attention in July, when the company announced it had raised more than $650 million in a funding round that valued it at around $9 billion.

claims.claim: Wonder aims to open more than 100 locations in Texas by the end of 2027.

evidence.quote: The company has outlined ambitious growth plans, including a major push into Texas, where it aims to open more than 100 locations by the end of 2027.

claims.claim: Wonder has acquired meal-kit company Blue Apron, restaurant delivery platform Grubhub, media company Tastemade, and kitchen robotics company Spyce.

evidence.quote: Additionally, Wonder has acquired meal-kit company Blue Apron, restaurant delivery platform Grubhub, media company Tastemade, and kitchen robotics company Spyce.

claims.claim: Wonder made a $425 million partnership with DoorDash to expand its campus dining business, which operates at 450 colleges and universities and other locations.
